findings.message: The ShortCode charset/length allowlist precondition (added by SECU-002) names only resolve and mark_taken_down. read_original_url also accepts an attacker-influenceable `code` ShortCode but is not listed under the defense-in-depth re-validation rule, so it is the one classified-read interface whose code argument is guarded solely by the parameterized PK lookup. By the SPEC's own stated defense-in-depth parity principle, the classified PII read deserves at least the same store-boundary code validation as the unprivileged resolve.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Section 5 ShortCode allowlist validation rule to include read_original_url (i.e., 'resolve, read_original_url, and mark_taken_down accept only a ShortCode matching the code-generation charset/length allowlist'), giving the highest-sensitivity read the same boundary precondition as the others.

findings.message: increment_visit accepts an EventId (`event_id`) that serves as the dedup/idempotency key, but no input-validation rule constrains its format/length. The dedup key is attacker-influenceable on the visit edge; an unbounded or malformed EventId could be used to bloat the dedup index or craft collisions against the idempotency gate. Risk is bounded because the consumer is idempotent and off the synchronous path, but no typed-parse/length rule is specified at the store boundary for this security-relevant key.
findings.recommendation: Add a Section 5 validation rule that increment_visit accepts only a typed/parsed EventId of bounded length/format (typed-parse or schema-validate) as a store-boundary precondition, paralleling the put_mapping OriginalUrl and resolve ShortCode allowlist rules.
